extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in comedy, late-night television, and entertainment news
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or performing late-night talk-show comedy and commentary about network decisions, politics, or cancellations—how hosts frame outrage, ridicule, and professionalism in monologues and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have fun with escalating silly ridicule
rubrics_metrics.description: “When the jerks are taking over, sometimes the best thing you can do is have fun coming up with increasingly silly ways to ridicule them.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use escalating silliness as a deliberate tactic to mock targets; the article frames this as a primary comedic strategy. Example: Letterman delights in inventing exaggerated nicknames rather than mounting a sober critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent misnaming / ridiculous nickname
rubrics_metrics.description: Letterman refers to the new Paramount boss David Ellison as “the Ellison Twins,” explaining, “I took great delight in referring to the principal as the Ellison Twins. I was later corrected and told it’s just one guy. I didn’t care and I still refer to him as twins.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning and sticking with a silly or demeaning nickname (even after correction) is presented as an effective comedic jab — it undercuts authority through absurdity and repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vivid insults and animalizing metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Letterman: “They’re lying. Let me just add one other thing… They’re lying weasels.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy vivid, concise insults or animal metaphors to express contempt and generate punchy lines. The article highlights direct name-calling as part of Letterman’s rhetorical toolbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deploy personal, sensory analogies to communicate outrage
rubrics_metrics.description: Letterman says the cancellation “feels like driving by your old neighborhood and realizing that where you used to live, they’re putting up an adult bookstore.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, relatable analogies grounded in personal feeling to dramatize loss or outrage; these help the audience emotionally connect and laugh at the incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a stoic, mournful tone when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert is described as “stoically mournful about the whole affair,” refusing to pin the cancellation solely on politics and instead processing it with measured grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A restrained, mournful tone can be an effective contrast to outrage-based comedy; it allows for reflection, irony, and dry humor rather than only invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge complexity — allow two truths at once
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert: “Maybe my cancellation was just a naturally occurring tumor… I would also say — and this is what feels most true to me — that two things can be true.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and voice nuance: combine systemic explanations (e.g., collapsing business model) with the possibility of targeted actions. This grants credibility and richer satire than simplistic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance critique with professional courtesy / maintain relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert recounts telling the Paramount chair that he wants to ‘make jokes about how this went down… I like working for CBS and I’m not going to change that relationship between now and the end if you allow that to happen.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the target is also a workplace or partner, negotiate a line between biting satire and preserving professional ties; this lets a host lampoon events while retaining future opportunities or dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dark or self-aware metaphors for dramatic comic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert’s line: “This lamb’s got a very cuttable throat.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ striking, even grim metaphors to convey vulnerability or sacrifice; when delivered with the right tone they create memorable, darkly comic moments that underline stakes.
